It will build an agentic AI system for operating the Advanced Rare Isotope Separator (ARIS) at FRIB. ARIS operations are limited by the gap between LISE++ simulations and observed beam behavior. As a result, weekly beam development takes 16 to 24 hours, about half of which goes to manual isotope calibration. Planning a new experiment takes about 20 days, and no predictive monitoring exists for roughly 200 time-correlated machine parameters. CLARA addresses this with three objectives: Planning and tuning. Bayesian optimization uses LISE++ as a physics-informed prior, alongside paired forward and inverse neural surrogates trained on simulation and EPICS archive data. These power a Planning Agent for non-experts and an Expert Tuning Agent. Calibration. Diffeomorphic image registration maps simulated particle identification (PID) distributions to measured ones from a single measurement. Monitoring and knowledge.
